title: Fitting singular subscheme of a nodal relative curve
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat, locally finitely presented morphism of schemes. Assume every nonempty geometric fibre is equidimensional of dimension $1$ and has only ordinary double point singularities (equivalently, at a singular geometric point its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ for an algebraically closed residue field $\Omega$). Let $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\hookrightarrow X$ be the first-Fitting singular subscheme [def-trf-first-fitting-singular-subscheme]. Then the relative smooth locus $U\subset X$ is open and the underlying set of $\operatorname{Sing}(f)$ is $X\setminus U$; $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\to S$ is unramified. For every morphism $S'\to S$, if $f':X\times_SS'\to S'$ is the base change, then the first-Fitting singular subscheme of $f'$ is canonically $\operatorname{Sing}(f)\times_SS'$ and its underlying set is the nonsmooth locus of $f'$.
